correctness.rationale: On z=(u,v,v,v,v) the weighted matrix gives the displayed two rows exactly. The largest eigenvalue of the full positive definite edge Gram matrix is (5+√17)/2 (the complementary eigenvalues to the two-coordinate restriction are 3,1,1). The derivative of the full lift is similar to I+h K_*^{1/2} diag(α,1,1,1,1) diag(cos z) K_*^{1/2}; the stipulated strict bound keeps it invertible for α near one. The torus map is homotopic to the identity and hence its local diffeomorphism has degree one. In w=u−v−π coordinates the exact update is w⁺=w+h[sin v−α sin(v+w)]. At α=1 the map on w=0 is v⁺=v+2h sin v, increasing on [0,π], with tangent multipliers 1+2h and 1−2h and normal multipliers 1−h and 1+h at the two endpoints, respectively. The local manifolds are smooth graphs over v; near each persistent endpoint the parameter derivative of the graph vanishes at the endpoint, and the derivative in v at α=1 is zero. This justifies the decaying boundary condition on the derivative along the moving perturbed half-orbit. Moving v makes no term in the normal derivative. Iterating W_{j+1}=a_jW_j−h sin(v_j) from the past gives a negative unstable contribution and solving backward from the future gives a positive stable contribution; the endpoint multipliers yield geometric tails. Smooth continuation to a transverse section gives a quadratic Taylor remainder with the indicated sign and order of subtraction.
residual_risks: No uniform detuning radius over h or endpoint sections, no conclusion on the full five-dimensional manifolds, and no reliance on the source floating-point diagnostic for the sign or series identity.
